sections.h2: Where is the Rockwall County Clerk's property records office?
sections.html:
Deeds, deeds of trust, liens and plats for Rockwall County are filed at the County Clerk's Property Department, 1111 E Yellowjacket Lane, Suite 100, Rockwall, TX 75087. The county's page warns that most GPS and internet maps place the building wrongly and says it sits about 0.3 miles east of Goliad and SH 205.

  • Phone: 972-204-6300. Fax: 972-204-6309.
  • Hours: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., except county holidays.
  • Cutoff: final transactions should be finished by 4 p.m.
  • ID: since House Bill 1195, a valid ID is required for any document presented in person to the Property Department.

The Official Public Records can be searched online, and copies and eCertified copies can be bought there. Paper certified copies are mailed by the clerk's office. A buyer who picks "In Person" can fill a cart online but must pay at the counter.

One caution applies to the online database. Under House Bill 4350, effective June 20, 2025, certain information is redacted from some instruments, and the county says the online database is not the official repository and may not show a record complete or unaltered. A title company works from the official records, so do not treat a screen search as the last word.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Rockwall County?
sections.html:
The clerk charges $25 for a first page and $4 for each page after that. Senate Bill 1612 repealed the old $1 filing fee under Local Government Code Section 291.008(d) from January 1, 2024, and the county's fee list reflects that repeal.

Rockwall County Clerk property records filing fees, as listed on the county's Property Records page
ItemFee
First page of a document$25
Each additional page$4
Each page of a plat$49
Each grantor or grantee above five names$0.25
UCC financing statement, 1 or 2 pages$35
UCC financing statement, more than 2 pages$50

Plats also require tax certificates, which are filed at their regular price. The county says it cannot refund an overpayment made by check. Ask the clerk's office what applies to your instrument before you send it.

sections.h2: What formatting rules does the Rockwall County Clerk enforce?
sections.html:
The clerk rejects documents more often for format than for substance. The county lists these general requirements:

  • Leave a blank 2-inch by 4-inch space at the bottom of the last page for the certification label. Without the space the label goes on the back, which creates an extra page and a $4 charge. The same rule covers e-filed documents.
  • Signatures must be originals or certified copies, since the clerk cannot file copies.
  • Print or type each name below its signature line.
  • An abstract of judgment must show the plaintiff's address or the fee is doubled.
  • A correction instrument has to conform to Texas Property Code Chapter 5.

A plat faces a longer checklist. It must be at least 18 by 24 inches and no larger than 24 by 36, with one black-line copy bearing original seals and signatures, a complete legal description, notarized signatures and a registered surveyor's certification. A plat inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction needs the city's approval, and every plat needs original tax certificates issued within 90 days of filing from all taxing units, showing no delinquent tax.

sections.h2: What does Texas law require before a deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
A deed or other conveyance of real property can be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged or sworn before a notary or other authorized officer, or before two subscribing witnesses (Property Code Section 12.001(b)). The county clerk acts as county recorder, and the record goes in the county where the land lies.

Estate paperwork also ends up in the clerk's files. A muniment of title order and the will are filed with the clerk of the county where the property sits. A transfer on death deed must be recorded before the owner dies. A small estate affidavit is for estates with no will and assets of $75,000 or less, not counting the homestead, and a homestead copy is recorded with the clerk. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement that no court has verified, and no law forces a lender or buyer to accept it.

For a seller with a title gap, the practical step is to pull the record chain early. A missing heir, an unreleased lien or an unrecorded deed shows up at the title company, and the fix usually means a new filing in this office.

sections.h2: How do foreclosure notices and mechanic's lien bonds work here?
sections.html:
The county posts foreclosure notices online. Trustee sales are held on the first Tuesday of the month on the front steps of the Rockwall County Courthouse, 1111 Yellowjacket Lane. The state requires the notice of sale at least 21 days ahead, posted at the courthouse door and filed with the clerk, and the sale runs between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. A borrower can reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days after the notice of default.

Mechanic's liens have an exit in this office. Under Property Code Sections 53.171 to 53.174, anyone may file a bond to indemnify against a lien, and the lien is discharged once a compliant bond is filed, notice goes to each claimant by certified mail, and the bond and notice are recorded. The bond must generally be double the lien amount, or when the claims top $40,000, the larger of 1.5 times the liens or $40,000 plus the liens. The clerk charges the usual $25 and $4 page fees, plus $1 a page for copies and the mailing postage.

The clerk also runs a free Property Fraud Alert that warns you by phone or email when a document is recorded under your name. A phone number can cover 3 names and an email address 4.

sections.h2: Who handles Rockwall County values and tax bills?
sections.html:
Values come from the Rockwall Central Appraisal District, 841 Justin Rd., Rockwall, 972-771-2034. The Comptroller's directory lists the county tax office at 101 E. Rusk St., Ste. 101, phone 972-204-6130, and says that office does not collect property tax. In that case the appraisal district may collect, so call it to learn where to pay.

The active units include Rockwall ISD and Royse City ISD, the cities of Rockwall, Fate, Royse City, Heath and McLendon-Chisholm, and parts of Wylie, Rowlett, Dallas and Garland. Seven municipal utility districts, three public improvement districts and the Club Municipal Management District #1 add more lines for some addresses.

A tax lien attaches on January 1, and the owner on that date is liable for the year's tax. State tax liens are recorded by the clerk in the state tax lien book. For city permits or code questions, the county says to call the municipality if the property lies inside city limits. Outside city limits, its Development Services department covers the county engineer, GIS and 911 addressing, environmental health, fire marshal, and road and bridge.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Rockwall County?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's Property Department, 1111 E Yellowjacket Lane, Suite 100, Rockwall, TX 75087. Bring a valid ID, since the county requires one for in-person filings, and plan to finish by 4 p.m.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Rockwall County?
faqs.a: The county lists $25 for the first page and $4 for each additional page. Add $0.25 for each grantor or grantee beyond five names, and extra if the last page lacks the 2-inch by 4-inch blank label space.

faqs.q: Can I search Rockwall County property records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The Official Public Records are searchable online, and copies can be bought there. The county says the online database is not the official repository because certain information is redacted, so use the clerk's office for certified records.

faqs.q: When are Rockwall County foreclosure sales held?
faqs.a: Trustee sales are on the first Tuesday of each month on the front steps of the Rockwall County Courthouse. Contact the trustee named on the notice with questions, and read the clerk's posted notices for the listings.

faqs.q: Does the Rockwall County tax office collect property tax?
faqs.a: The Comptroller's directory says it does not, and that the appraisal district may collect instead. Call the Rockwall Central Appraisal District at 972-771-2034 to confirm where your bill is paid.
